A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IWAE multi-sample objective is not the best objective to optimise for importance-weighted autoencoder models.

AISLE is a more flexible, general and theoretically sound framework than IWAE, which allows for the use of any reparametrisable distribution (including the standard Gaussian), and which can be used to derive IWAE-type objectives as special cases.
AISLE is the generalised version of IWAE which avoids its gradient breakdown.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IWAE objective is not a good objective to optimise and that the RWS algorithm (or a similar algorithm) is preferable.
